title: Unconditional State Transitions
pattern: A method that mutates a system's state or inventory blindly on call without validating current state constraints or preconditions.
why_bad: It permits the system to enter invalid states (e.g., dispensing cash when the account is overdrawn or the machine is empty) because the code treats state machines as simple sequential actions [67:67].
detection: State-changing functions that do not verify the current state invariants before writing to local state fields [67:67].
fix: Implement explicit guard assertions or type-driven state machines to enforce valid state transitions [67:67].
